safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes E45 being ineffective but does not mention antihistamines.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the patient also tried antihistamines does not materially change the likely diagnosis (contact/irritant dermatitis) or the core management plan (trigger avoidance, emollients, topical steroid). At most it could lead to redundant advice to try antihistamines again, with minimal clinical impact.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document NKDA leaves allergy status uncertain in the record, which can delay prescribing/dispensing or reduce safety checking when new medications (e.g., topical steroids or other treatments) are initiated. While it does not introduce a false allergy, missing allergy documentation is clinically relevant and can contribute to preventable workflow and safety risks.
